chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Asbaat, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said:
I prayed behind Al-Rida (peace be upon him) in the Sacred Masjid, the night prayer. So when he was free, he made the place of rest a prostration.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (a title for Imam Ali ibn Musa)
key_terms.الضَّجْعَةِ: The place of rest (a sitting position between prostrations or after prayer)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Rida do with the place of rest after completing the night prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the unique liturgical practice of Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who substituted the traditional sitting position (daj'ah) with an additional prostration (sajdah) during the night prayer. This variation underscores the scholarly discussion regarding the permissibility and merit of adding voluntary prostrations in optional prayers, reflecting the Imam's adherence to the Prophet's Sunnah while demonstrating personal spiritual depth. It serves as a key reference in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the flexibility in the structure of *Salat al-Layl*.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Asbaat, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al-Balaad who said,
‘I prayed Salāt behind Al-Rezaasws in the Sacred Masjid, the night Salāt. So when heasws was free, heasws made the place of rest as a Sajdah’.
en.sarwar: 26. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Asbat from Ibrahim ibn abu al-Balad who has said the following: “

I performed my Salah (prayer), in Masjid al-Haram. Al-Rida’ ‘Alayhi al-Salam, led the Salah (prayer). It was Salah (prayer) of night. When he (the Imam) completed, he (the Imam) made his sleep (instead of sleeping after Salah (prayer)) into a Sajdah (prostration).”
